hypothesis: The useful FURNISHER/INTERPHASE composition law can be expressed more clearly with ordinary HTML than with a custom infinite-canvas editor: DOM nesting is composition, native <details> is fold/unfold, visible links are seams, and the runtime interprets that same markup.
correction: SPACE SCALE 0.2 made composition executable but hid the program in a separate JavaScript graph model.
That weakened the historical 'homoiconic interface language' aspiration and made the interface harder to understand.
0.3 removes the separate graph model from the current surface.
laws: DOCUMENT = PROGRAM STRUCTURE: #program DOM is the canonical composition.
NESTING = COMPOSITION: a composite is ordinary nested HTML.
DETAILS = FOLD: closing/opening a <details> element changes abstraction visibility without changing identity.
LINK = SEAM: ordinary href anchors are both visible navigation and executable next edges.
SOURCE = SAME OBJECT: SOURCE edits and reapplies the exact #program markup, not a second serialized graph.
RETURN = MARKUP + TRACE: RETURN records the same HTML plus runtime evidence.
NO STRICT HOMOICONICITY CLAIM: behavior is still interpreted by JavaScript; call this DOM-as-program / structurally reflexive.
PHYSICAL REALITY REMAINS EXTERNAL: no fit/load/safety inference.
implemented: Traditional linear HTML document with native details/summary folding.
Nested FURNISHER COMPILER block whose children are its visible implementation.
Visible rel=next anchors used by RUN as the execution path.
Small safe interpreter for SOURCE / WRAP / GROUP / CONFIG / COMPILE / VERIFY / RETURN.
SOURCE panel exposes the exact live #program outerHTML and can reapply edited markup.
RETURN captures live markup and execution trace.
Direct links to the preserved 0.2 canvas and 0.1 cube for comparison.
boundaries: HTML+JavaScript is not strictly homoiconic in the Lisp sense.
The current claim is narrower: structural representation and executable composition share the DOM tree and visible links.
No custom node editor, pan/zoom substrate, drag graph or hidden topology is required for current use.
evidence_gate: A new user should be able to understand the current composition by reading the page, open/close the compiler block without instructions, follow visible seams, run it, inspect SOURCE, and explain what structure RUN interpreted. If not, simplify again.
next_if_pass: Use the DOM-as-program pattern on one real small FIELD transformation. Only reintroduce richer projections as optional views over the same HTML structure.
next_if_fail: Reduce further to static HTML + links; keep the interpreter optional.
